newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Iama profits up despite tough conditions.
newsitem.headline: Iama profits up despite tough conditions.

text.p: Rural services group Iama Ltd said on Tuesday its half-year results had been hampered by difficult trading conditions and dry weather and that the nine percent increase in net earnings was a good outcome considering this.
Iama earlier reported a net profit of A$6.81 million for the six months to March 31, up from A$6.23 million a year earlier.
"Low insect pressure in New South Wales and Queensland also affected our profits through reduced demand for crop protection products," managing director Danny Bourke said in a statement.
Sales rose 14 percent to A$419 million, but nine percent of this related to acquisitions of new businesses which were expected to deliver profits in the second half, Bourke said.

Acquisitions during the period included Chemstock Animal Health, a veterinary distribution company in New Zealand, Carr Bros in New South Wales, and 80 percent of Franklin Smith in Victoria. In a move to improve downstream marketing services for growers, Iama also bought Aussigold. The company packs, markets
and exports produce from its base in North Queensland.

"Iama's aim is to expand this operation into other regions of Australia," the company said. It said the company's immediate focus would be on sales opportunities following a strong start to the winter cropping season in most states.

"Continued rationalisation of our operations will reduce costs in the short to medium term and profit improvements are also being pursued, particularily in the area of working capital management," Bourke said.
Iama also said it aimed to build on initiatives including expansion of services on irrigation, international distribution rights to new seed varieties and a new range of "house branded" products.
